assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope covers RLHF, DPO/IPO/KTO/ORPO, reward modeling, preference data collection, RLVR, and reward hacking mitigation
a supervised fine-tuned (SFT) baseline is assumed as starting point for alignment
compute and annotation budgets are finite; tradeoffs between methods are real engineering constraints
exclusions: base model pre-training and architecture design
inference serving infrastructure and latency engineering

competency_questions.question: What preference data collection protocol (annotation format, elicitation method, quality threshold) is used?
How is prompt diversity managed to prevent narrow alignment?
What reward model architecture and loss function are used and how is the RM evaluated?
How does the RLHF PPO training loop incorporate the reward model and KL constraint?
How is reward hacking detected and mitigated throughout alignment training?
How does DPO eliminate the explicit reward model and what are its failure modes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DPO node defines objective and failure modes

competency_questions.question: What alignment variants beyond DPO (IPO, KTO, ORPO) exist and when are they preferred?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IPO_KTO_ORPO defines variants and selection criteria

competency_questions.question: How does RLVR apply verifiable rewards for math and code without a learned reward model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RLVR node defines verifiable reward approach

competency_questions.question: How do process reward models provide step-level supervision for chain-of-thought?
How is alignment quality evaluated beyond reward scores to avoid Goodhart inflation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PREF_EVAL and GOODHART_MONITOR define multi-metric eval

competency_questions.question: How does iterative/online RLHF address distribution mismatch between RM and policy?
How are safety alignment and harmlessness integrated without causing over-refusal?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAFETY_ALIGN defines harmlessness training with over-refusal mitigation

competency_questions.question: What base model selection criteria govern the alignment pipeline entry point?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BASE_MODEL_SELECT defines criteria including license constraints

competency_questions.question: How is compute budget allocated across SFT, RM training, RLHF rollouts, and DPO?

glossary.definition: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: fine-tuning LLMs using a reward model trained on human preferences, optimized via PPO
Direct Preference Optimization: closed-form alignment objective that implicitly defines a reward through the policy ratio without explicit RM
policy behavior that maximizes the proxy reward model without satisfying the true human preference
Kullback-Leibler divergence used as a penalty to bound policy drift from the reference (SFT) policy during RLHF
Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards: RL using ground-truth-checkable rewards instead of learned reward models
Preference elicitation protocol where annotators write a rationale before selecting a preferred response, reducing noise
Reward model that scores individual reasoning steps rather than only final outputs, providing dense supervision
When a proxy measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure of the true objective - the central alignment risk in RLHF
Supervised Fine-Tuning: fine-tuning on instruction-demonstration pairs via cross-entropy; prerequisite and reference for alignment methods

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for preference alignment work units derived from published literature on RLHF, DPO, InstructGPT, and related alignment research in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Ouyang et al. 2022 InstructGPT; Rafailov et al. 2023 DPO; Christiano et al. 2017 RLHF; Lambert RLHF Book

nodes.definition: Design and execute human (or AI-assisted) preference data collection: binary comparisons, explain-then-choose elicitation, Likert ratings, and multi-annotator adjudication to build a high-signal training corpus for reward modeling and direct alignment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: annotation guidelines revised or annotator pool changes

pros.claim: Explain-then-choose elicitation improves annotator coherence and reduces noise
pros.example: Annotators who write rationale before choosing produce higher agreement (Ouyang et al. 2022)

cons.claim: Human annotation is expensive, slow, and subject to position and verbosity biases
cons.example: Annotators favor longer responses even when shorter is better

acceptance_tests: inter-annotator agreement kappa>=0.6 on held-out sample
no statistically significant position-order effect detected

nodes.definition: Train a scalar reward model (RM) from preference comparison data using a Bradley-Terry pairwise ranking loss; the RM maps (prompt, response) to a scalar reward used to drive RLHF policy optimization.

excluded: DPO which has no explicit RM

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reward hacking detected or new preference data collected

pros.claim: Centralizes human preference signal into a differentiable surrogate
pros.example: RM enables gradient-based RL policy optimization

cons.claim: RM overfitting to annotator artifacts causes reward hacking downstream
cons.example: RM trained on verbosity bias produces sycophantic policy

failure_modes: distributional mismatch between RM training and RL rollouts
acceptance_tests: RM accuracy >=65% on held-out comparisons
reward score rank-correlates with human preference on audit sample
no reward distribution collapse observed
revisit_triggers: reward hacking signal detected in RLHF run
RM accuracy drops >5% on new prompt domain

nodes.definition: Fine-tune a language model policy via Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) using a learned reward model signal plus KL penalty against a reference policy to prevent mode collapse and reward hacking.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reward hacking detected, KL divergence exceeds budget, or policy collapses

pros.claim: State-of-the-art alignment quality when tuned correctly; InstructGPT showed large win-rate gains over SFT
pros.example: InstructGPT PPO outperformed 175B SFT on human evals at 1.3B scale

cons.claim: Extremely complex; requires reward model, value head, rollouts, KL tuning - high engineering cost
cons.example: PPO instability requires careful learning rate, batch size, and KL coefficient sweep

acceptance_tests: KL vs reference policy within budget [0.02,0.2] throughout training
reward score improves monotonically for at least first 2k steps
human eval win-rate vs SFT baseline >=55%
revisit_triggers: reward hacking signal in rollout audits
human eval win-rate drops below SFT baseline
policy generates harmful outputs at audit

nodes.definition: Fine-tune a base LLM on curated instruction-following demonstrations via standard cross-entropy to produce an SFT model that serves as the starting point for preference alignment methods.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: base model updated or instruction data distribution changes

pros.claim: SFT warm-start dramatically improves alignment stability vs training from base
pros.example: RLHF from SFT reaches better final reward than from base in InstructGPT ablation

cons.claim: SFT alone produces sycophantic or over-compliant models if demonstration data is biased
cons.example: SFT on contractor data overrepresents verbose, agreeable outputs

acceptance_tests: eval loss converges without oscillation
MT-Bench or instruction-following benchmark score > base model

nodes.definition: Optimize a language model policy directly on preference pairs using the DPO closed-form objective that implicitly defines a reward through the policy ratio, eliminating the need for an explicit reward model or RL loop.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new preference data collected or alignment quality regression observed

pros.claim: Eliminates reward model training and RL loop; substantially simpler pipeline
pros.example: DPO achieves competitive win-rates vs PPO with 2-3x less compute (Rafailov et al. 2023)

cons.claim: Implicit reward not directly inspectable; harder to diagnose reward hacking
cons.example: Policy may drift to degenerate responses when beta is too low

failure_modes: chosen response probability decreasing (DPO likelihood displacement)
distribution shift between SFT and preference data
acceptance_tests: chosen response log-prob increases relative to SFT
rejected response log-prob decreases relative to SFT
no catastrophic forgetting on base capability benchmarks
revisit_triggers: preference data OOD from SFT distribution

nodes.definition: Apply alignment variants beyond DPO: IPO (identity preference optimization), KTO (Kahneman-Tversky optimization using binary desirability labels), and ORPO (odds-ratio preference optimization fusing SFT and alignment in one stage).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new alignment loss variant published or data format constraint changes

pros.claim: KTO avoids paired comparison data requirement, enabling alignment from binary labels
pros.example: KTO applicable where comparison pairs are infeasible to collect

cons.claim: Variant choice is domain-sensitive; no universally dominant choice
cons.example: IPO may under-optimize on tasks with clear verifiable rewards

failure_modes: ORPO requiring careful SFT loss weighting
acceptance_tests: chosen variant evaluated against DPO baseline on target benchmark
alignment gain measured on held-out human eval
revisit_triggers: new variant with strong empirical results published

nodes.definition: Apply reinforcement learning with verifiable process or outcome rewards (RLVR) for domains where correctness can be checked automatically (math, code, formal verification), bypassing learned reward models entirely.
inputs: verifiable reward function (unit tests, math checker)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: verifiable reward domain expands or solve-rate plateaus

pros.claim: Avoids reward model entirely for math/code; reward signal is ground truth
pros.example: DeepSeek-R1 and similar models show RLVR enables superhuman math solve rates

cons.claim: Limited to domains with cheap, reliable automated verification
cons.example: Verification function bugs become adversarial reward sources

failure_modes: distributional collapse on non-verifiable prompt types
acceptance_tests: solve rate on held-out problem set improves vs SFT baseline
no test-case hacking detected in rollout audit
model generalizes to unseen problem variants

nodes.definition: Detect and mitigate reward hacking through KL constraints, ensemble RMs, iterative human audits, and conservative early stopping to ensure the policy improves true human preference, not just the proxy reward.

included: reward score vs human preference gap

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new reward hacking pattern discovered or KL divergence exceeds threshold

pros.claim: KL penalty plus early stopping is most reliable single mitigation for reward hacking
pros.example: InstructGPT used KL to prevent mode collapse throughout RL training

cons.claim: No mitigation eliminates hacking completely; RM faithfulness is bounded by training data
cons.example: Ensemble RMs reduce but do not eliminate Goodhart failures

failure_modes: ignoring rollout audits until late training
KL too loose allowing full hacking
acceptance_tests: human preference win-rate tracks reward score correlation >=0.7 throughout training
no flagged hacking behaviors in rollout audit sample
KL remains within configured budget
revisit_triggers: human auditors flag new hacking pattern

nodes.definition: Evaluate alignment quality using human win-rate comparisons, LLM-as-judge panels, adversarial red-teaming, and established benchmarks (MT-Bench, AlpacaEval, TruthfulQA) to measure progress without Goodhart inflation.
inputs: human rater pool or LLM judge

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: benchmark saturation detected or judge bias discovered

pros.claim: Multi-metric eval (human + LLM judge + red-team) resists single-metric Goodharting
pros.example: AlpacaEval length-bias corrected version reduced spurious score inflation

cons.claim: LLM-as-judge has verbosity and self-preference biases; human eval is expensive
cons.example: GPT-4 judge prefers GPT-4 outputs, inflating win-rates against GPT-4-aligned models

acceptance_tests: human win-rate and LLM-judge win-rate correlate >=0.7
red-team pass rate <5% on harm categories
length-controlled eval shows no significant verbosity artifact

nodes.definition: Run multiple rounds of preference data collection, reward model refinement, and policy optimization (online RLHF / RLAIF) where each round uses the current policy to generate candidates for human or AI feedback, improving data coverage iteratively.

included: online preference collection from policy rollouts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: policy distribution shifts enough to invalidate offline RM

pros.claim: Online feedback on policy rollouts corrects distribution mismatch that offline methods miss
pros.example: RLAIF scales feedback collection using AI raters cost-effectively

cons.claim: Compounding errors across rounds if RM is not refreshed; high infrastructure cost
cons.example: Each iteration requires rollout generation, rating, and retraining pipeline

failure_modes: RM staleness causing feedback on outdated distribution
acceptance_tests: per-round win-rate improves or plateaus within tolerance
RM refreshed before distribution gap exceeds threshold
round convergence detected within N rounds
revisit_triggers: distribution gap between RM training and current policy exceeds threshold

nodes.definition: Apply Constitutional AI (CAI) or RLAIF to generate and filter preference data using AI feedback from a set of principles (the constitution), reducing dependence on human annotators for harmlessness and helpfulness labeling.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: constitution updated or AI judge model changed

pros.claim: Scales harmlessness labeling without large human annotation budget
pros.example: Anthropic CAI reduced harmful outputs at scale without proportional human label cost

cons.claim: AI judge inherits biases of judge model; constitution may miss novel harm categories
cons.example: Circular feedback if judge model is the same family as model being trained

acceptance_tests: harmlessness eval pass rate improves over SFT baseline
AI judge preference distribution matches human judge on audit sample >=0.65 kappa

nodes.definition: Configure and monitor the KL divergence penalty between the optimizing policy and a frozen reference policy to bound policy drift, prevent reward hacking, and maintain base-model capabilities during alignment training.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: KL budget breached or capability regression detected

pros.claim: KL penalty is the primary mechanism preventing reward hacking and capability degradation
pros.example: InstructGPT ablation: removing KL caused mode collapse and hacking

cons.claim: Too-tight KL prevents alignment learning; too-loose allows hacking; requires empirical tuning
cons.example: Beta schedule interacts with reward scale in non-obvious ways

failure_modes: KL too tight preventing reward learning
acceptance_tests: KL stays within configured budget throughout training
base capability benchmarks (MMLU) do not regress >3%
reward signal improves despite KL constraint

nodes.definition: Filter and curate preference datasets by removing low-agreement pairs, near-duplicate prompts, annotation artifacts (length bias, formatting bias), and harmful content to ensure downstream reward model and DPO training quality.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new annotation artifact discovered or upstream data pipeline changes

pros.claim: Removing low-agreement pairs improves RM accuracy more than adding noisy pairs
pros.example: Filtering to kappa>=0.6 pairs improves RM held-out accuracy significantly in practice

cons.claim: Aggressive filtering reduces dataset size; bias in filtering criteria can skew distribution
cons.example: Filtering on agreement may systematically remove hard but important examples

acceptance_tests: filtered dataset IAA >= threshold
no statistically significant length bias in chosen vs rejected
toxic content scan pass rate 100%
revisit_triggers: dataset size drops below minimum for RM training

nodes.definition: Design and manage the prompt distribution for preference data collection and RL training to maximize coverage of user intents, domains, difficulty levels, and adversarial cases, preventing narrow alignment that fails on distribution shift.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: traffic distribution shifts or new user domain discovered

pros.claim: Diverse prompt distribution prevents narrow alignment that fails on novel user intents
pros.example: InstructGPT used labeler-written diverse prompts to cover breadth of intents

cons.claim: Adversarial prompt inclusion can shift training distribution toward edge cases
cons.example: Balancing coverage vs depth is task-specific and hard to optimize globally

failure_modes: prompt distribution dominated by easy/common cases
adversarial prompts over-represented causing spurious safety behavior
acceptance_tests: coverage metric spans all defined intent categories
diversity coefficient >= threshold
no domain constitutes >30% of prompt pool without justification

nodes.definition: Select the base model for alignment fine-tuning by evaluating capability-alignment tradeoffs, license/ToS constraints (open vs gated weights), compute budget, and context-length requirements before committing to a fine-tuning path.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new base model released or license terms change

pros.claim: Committing to a capable base model with permissive license prevents downstream legal and capability blockers
pros.example: LLaMA 2/3 community license enabled broad fine-tuning research without gated-API cost

cons.claim: Irreversible early choice: downstream fine-tuning investment lost if base model changes
cons.example: Switching base models mid-project requires restarting SFT and alignment from scratch

failure_modes: base model capability insufficient for target task
context length mismatch with deployment requirements
acceptance_tests: legal sign-off on license terms before training begins
base capability benchmarks meet minimum thresholds
compute cost within budget
revisit_triggers: capability regression in base model update
new model significantly outperforms on target tasks

nodes.definition: Monitor for Goodhart's Law effects where optimizing a proxy measure diverges from the true objective through periodic human audits, benchmark rotation, capability regression tests, and out-of-distribution probes.

included: reward score vs human preference correlation tracking

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reward vs human preference decorrelation detected or benchmark contamination suspected

pros.claim: Proactive Goodhart monitoring catches overfitting before deployment
pros.example: Periodic human audit halts training before hacking compounds into deployment failures

cons.claim: Goodhart effects are domain-specific and hard to detect automatically; false-negative risk
cons.example: Contamination detection requires withheld benchmark versions which are operationally expensive

failure_modes: monitoring too infrequent to catch early hacking
OOD probe set not covering actual distribution shift
acceptance_tests: reward vs human preference Pearson r >= 0.7 throughout training
benchmark contamination scan returns no hits
OOD probe pass rate >= baseline
revisit_triggers: public benchmark included in training data

nodes.definition: Train or apply process reward models (PRMs) that score individual reasoning steps rather than final outputs only, enabling fine-grained supervision of chain-of-thought reasoning for math, code, and multi-step problems.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: step labeling quality degrades or new reasoning domain added

pros.claim: Step-level supervision provides denser reward signal and catches early reasoning errors
pros.example: Let's Verify Step by Step showed PRM outperforms ORM on MATH benchmark

cons.claim: Step-level annotation is far more expensive than outcome labeling; step boundary definition is ambiguous
cons.example: Step boundary ambiguity makes PRM training noisy on free-form reasoning

failure_modes: step boundary ambiguity causing noisy labels
PRM rewarding verbose but wrong steps
annotation cost prohibitive for large step-labeled datasets
acceptance_tests: step reward correlates with final correctness >=0.65
PRM-guided best-of-N improves solve rate vs outcome-RM best-of-N on held-out problems
revisit_triggers: new reasoning domain with different step structure

nodes.definition: Incorporate explicit safety training into the alignment pipeline: harmlessness preference data, refusal training, red-team attack coverage, and safety-specific RLHF or DPO passes to reduce harmful output rates without excessive over-refusal.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new attack vector discovered or over-refusal rate exceeds threshold

pros.claim: Dedicated safety pass substantially reduces harmful output rates
pros.example: Anthropic Harmless RLHF reduced toxic output rates dramatically on ToxiGen-style probes

cons.claim: Safety-helpfulness tension: over-indexing on harmlessness causes over-refusal and unhelpfulness
cons.example: Excessive refusal on benign prompts reduces user trust and product utility

failure_modes: safety training removing capabilities needed for helpfulness
red-team coverage gaps leaving novel attack vectors unmitigated
acceptance_tests: harmful output rate < target threshold on red-team probe set
over-refusal rate < 5% on benign helpfulness benchmark
helpfulness score does not regress vs pre-safety-pass baseline by >5%

nodes.definition: Generate synthetic preference pairs and demonstrations using stronger models (or self-play) to augment or replace costly human annotation, including reject-sampling fine-tuning (RFT) and AI-generated comparison data.

included: teacher model distillation into preference format

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: teacher model updated or quality filter detects distribution collapse

pros.claim: Scales preference data 10-100x at low cost; RFT enables curriculum from best rollouts
pros.example: RFT on filtered model rollouts gave significant MATH improvement cheaply

cons.claim: Risk of mode collapse if synthetic data distribution is narrow; teacher model biases propagate
cons.example: Synthetic pairs from same model family create circular training signal

failure_modes: quality filter too permissive admitting noise
acceptance_tests: synthetic dataset diversity metric >= human dataset baseline
RM trained on synthetic+human outperforms human-only on held-out eval
quality filter removes >=threshold of low-scoring pairs
revisit_triggers: downstream RM or DPO quality regresses

nodes.definition: Plan and manage GPU compute budgets for the full alignment pipeline including SFT, RM training, RLHF rollouts, DPO, and evaluation, accounting for iteration costs, rollout overhead, and the substantially higher RLHF cost vs SFT.

included: cost comparison SFT vs RLHF vs DPO

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pipeline stage costs change or model size changes

pros.claim: DPO reduces alignment compute 3-5x vs PPO-RLHF; knowing this drives architecture choice
pros.example: Budget planning reveals that RL rollout generation dominates RLHF cost

cons.claim: Compute estimates for RLHF are highly sensitive to rollout length; hard to estimate a priori
cons.example: Underestimating rollout cost causes mid-training budget overruns

failure_modes: insufficient memory for reference+policy model in same run
acceptance_tests: compute estimate within 20% of actual for each stage on dry run
GPU memory fits reference+policy+optimizer without OOM
budget approved before training begins

nodes.definition: Implement deployment-time guardrails for aligned models: input/output classifiers, Constitutional AI filters, refusal rate monitoring, and anomaly detection to catch misalignment failures not caught in offline evaluation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new attack vector in production or refusal rate anomaly detected

pros.claim: Defense-in-depth: deployment classifiers catch misalignment missed in offline eval
pros.example: Production anomaly detection caught distribution shift within hours of deployment rollout

cons.claim: Guardrails add latency; over-filtering causes false positives that degrade user experience
cons.example: Deployment classifier adversarially targeted once deployed at scale

failure_modes: false positive rate causing over-refusal in production
monitoring gap between deployment and anomaly detection
acceptance_tests: guardrail latency p99 < threshold
false positive rate on benign traffic < 2%
anomaly detection alert latency < 1 hour

edges.why_related: annotation output feeds directly into quality filtering
edges.risk_of_conflict: noisy annotations degrade RM quality
edges.resolution_rule: run filtering immediately after annotation batch

edges.why_related: RM training requires preference comparison data
edges.risk_of_conflict: RM trained on noisy data produces misaligned rewards
edges.resolution_rule: finalize data quality before RM training

edges.why_related: DPO requires chosen/rejected preference pairs
edges.risk_of_conflict: DPO with noisy pairs produces poor alignment
edges.resolution_rule: filter pairs before DPO training

edges.why_related: filtered dataset used for RM training
edges.risk_of_conflict: noisy data hurts RM generalization
edges.resolution_rule: use filtered dataset for RM

edges.why_related: filtered pairs feed DPO training
edges.risk_of_conflict: noisy pairs cause DPO displacement
edges.resolution_rule: use filtered pairs for DPO

edges.why_related: prompt distribution shapes coverage of annotation
edges.risk_of_conflict: narrow prompts cause narrow alignment
edges.resolution_rule: finalize prompt distribution before starting annotation

edges.why_related: SFT checkpoint used as RM base model
edges.risk_of_conflict: RM from base model converges slower
edges.resolution_rule: train SFT before RM

edges.why_related: RLHF starts from SFT policy
edges.risk_of_conflict: RL from base model diverges
edges.resolution_rule: SFT must complete before PPO

edges.why_related: DPO requires SFT model as reference and init
edges.risk_of_conflict: DPO without SFT reference diverges
edges.resolution_rule: SFT must complete before DPO

edges.why_related: RLVR commonly starts from SFT policy for reasoning domains
edges.risk_of_conflict: RLVR from base diverges on hard reasoning tasks
edges.resolution_rule: complete SFT before RLVR

edges.why_related: PPO requires RM to generate reward signal
edges.risk_of_conflict: RL without RM has no differentiable signal
edges.resolution_rule: train and validate RM before PPO

edges.why_related: RM overfitting is the primary source of reward hacking
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmonitored RM causes hacking
edges.example: RM accuracy vs human preference gap
edges.resolution_rule: monitor RM during and after RLHF

edges.why_related: hacking manifests in RLHF rollouts
edges.risk_of_conflict: unchecked PPO produces hacking at scale
edges.resolution_rule: monitor for hacking throughout RLHF

edges.why_related: RLHF policy is the primary artifact evaluated
edges.risk_of_conflict: eval without RLHF baseline is uninformative
edges.resolution_rule: evaluate after each RLHF checkpoint

edges.why_related: DPO policy requires same eval protocol as RLHF
edges.risk_of_conflict: separate eval protocols prevent fair comparison
edges.resolution_rule: use consistent eval protocol for both DPO and RLHF

edges.why_related: RLVR policy evaluated on held-out math/code benchmarks
edges.risk_of_conflict: benchmark contamination inflates RLVR eval
edges.resolution_rule: use held-out benchmarks not seen in training

edges.why_related: KL constraint directly bounds PPO policy update
edges.risk_of_conflict: unconstrained PPO diverges or hacks
edges.example: KL penalty coefficient in PPO objective
edges.resolution_rule: set KL budget before RLHF training starts

edges.why_related: reference policy for KL is the SFT checkpoint
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong reference causes miscalibrated KL
edges.resolution_rule: freeze SFT before using as KL reference

edges.why_related: hacking mitigation feeds into broader Goodhart monitoring
edges.risk_of_conflict: monitoring only reward hacking misses benchmark Goodhart
edges.resolution_rule: run Goodhart monitor as superset of hacking detection

edges.why_related: eval results are primary input to Goodhart risk assessment
edges.benefit_of_coupling: links proxy metrics to true objective
edges.risk_of_conflict: eval used without Goodhart check inflates confidence
edges.example: benchmark score vs human preference gap
edges.resolution_rule: always follow eval with Goodhart risk review

edges.why_related: online RLHF requires iterative RM refresh to match policy distribution
edges.risk_of_conflict: stale RM evaluates wrong policy distribution
edges.resolution_rule: retrain RM whenever distribution gap exceeds threshold

edges.why_related: online rounds require new preference data from current policy rollouts
edges.risk_of_conflict: reusing offline data for online rounds causes distribution mismatch
edges.resolution_rule: collect new preference data from policy rollouts per round

edges.why_related: CAI generates preference labels replacing or augmenting human annotation
edges.risk_of_conflict: AI-generated labels propagate judge model bias
edges.resolution_rule: audit AI labels against human sample before full replacement

edges.why_related: constitutional principles inform safety alignment priorities
edges.risk_of_conflict: safety training without constitution lacks coherent value specification
edges.resolution_rule: use constitution to scope safety training

edges.why_related: safety training informs deployment classifier thresholds
edges.risk_of_conflict: deployment guardrails miscalibrated without safety training context
edges.example: harm category taxonomy from safety training
edges.resolution_rule: calibrate deployment classifiers using safety training outcomes

edges.why_related: offline eval results set thresholds for deployment monitoring
edges.risk_of_conflict: deployment threshold set without offline eval baseline
edges.resolution_rule: use offline eval baselines to calibrate deployment thresholds

edges.why_related: base model choice determines SFT architecture and tokenizer
edges.risk_of_conflict: base model change invalidates SFT checkpoint
edges.resolution_rule: finalize base model before SFT design

edges.why_related: model size determines compute requirements for all alignment stages
edges.risk_of_conflict: underestimating compute for chosen model size
edges.resolution_rule: finalize model choice before compute planning

edges.why_related: RLHF compute budget constrains iteration count and rollout length
edges.risk_of_conflict: PPO halted mid-training due to budget exhaustion
edges.resolution_rule: set rollout budget before starting PPO

edges.why_related: DPO budget enables choosing between DPO and RLHF
edges.benefit_of_coupling: lower cost of DPO drives adoption
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing RLHF without DPO cost comparison wastes budget
edges.resolution_rule: compare compute cost before choosing alignment algorithm

edges.why_related: PRM provides step-level signal complementary to RLVR outcome rewards
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflicting step and outcome rewards confuse policy
edges.example: PRM as dense reward in MCTS
edges.resolution_rule: ensure PRM and outcome rewards are consistent before combining

edges.why_related: outcome RM provides baseline; PRM adds step granularity
edges.risk_of_conflict: PRM trained without outcome RM baseline has no quality anchor
edges.example: outcome RM accuracy informs PRM scope
edges.resolution_rule: train outcome RM first, then add PRM for step-level supervision

edges.why_related: IPO/KTO/ORPO are competing objectives to DPO; choice conflicts when both applied
edges.risk_of_conflict: applying both DPO and IPO with different objectives contradicts
edges.resolution_rule: select one primary alignment loss; treat others as baselines

edges.why_related: synthetic preference data augments human annotation
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthetic data displacing human data causing bias propagation
edges.resolution_rule: maintain human annotation as quality anchor; use synthetic for scale

edges.why_related: synthetic pairs included in RM training data
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthetic data quality degrades RM if not filtered
edges.resolution_rule: filter synthetic pairs before including in RM training

edges.why_related: Goodhart monitoring triggers new alignment rounds when proxy diverges
edges.risk_of_conflict: Goodhart failure compounds if monitoring does not trigger retraining
edges.resolution_rule: trigger new alignment round when Goodhart monitor fires

edges.why_related: human annotation establishes quality baseline for synthetic generation
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthetic without human anchor produces uncontrolled distribution
edges.resolution_rule: collect human baseline before generating synthetic at scale

edges.why_related: safety alignment and helpfulness optimization tension within RLHF
edges.risk_of_conflict: unconstrained helpfulness reward suppresses safety
edges.resolution_rule: tune safety and helpfulness reward weights jointly; monitor both

edges.why_related: production anomalies trigger Goodhart review of offline eval metrics
edges.risk_of_conflict: production signal ignored causing Goodhart inflation to persist
edges.resolution_rule: route production anomalies to Goodhart monitor

conflict_axes.description: Full RLHF (PPO+RM) achieves higher peak alignment quality but requires 5-10x engineering complexity and compute vs DPO; teams must choose based on quality target and resource budget
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use DPO for resource-constrained settings; use RLHF when peak alignment quality is required and budget allows

conflict_axes.description: Human preference annotation provides high-quality ground truth but is expensive and slow; synthetic data scales cheaply but risks bias propagation and mode collapse
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use human annotation as quality anchor; augment with synthetic only after quality gate passes

conflict_axes.description: Optimizing for harmlessness via safety RLHF reduces harmful outputs but increases over-refusal; optimizing purely for helpfulness risks safety failures
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tune safety and helpfulness reward weights jointly; monitor both metrics throughout training

conflict_axes.description: Tight KL constraint prevents reward hacking but also limits alignment improvement; loose KL enables faster learning but risks mode collapse and hacking
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: start with moderate KL; adapt using monitored reward-preference correlation

conflict_axes.description: Offline alignment (one-shot DPO/RLHF) is simpler but suffers distribution mismatch; online iterative RLHF is more powerful but requires continuous data collection and RM refresh infrastructure
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use offline for initial alignment; add online rounds only when distribution mismatch is confirmed

conflict_axes.description: Outcome-only reward models are cheaper to train but miss reasoning errors in intermediate steps; process reward models provide denser signal but require expensive step-level annotation
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use outcome RM as baseline; add PRM for math/code domains where step quality is critical

conflict_axes.description: Learned RMs are flexible but subject to Goodhart/hacking; verifiable rewards are ground-truth accurate but only applicable to domains with cheap automated checking
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use RLVR wherever verification is available; use learned RM for subjective or open-ended tasks

conflict_axes.description: Larger base models achieve higher alignment quality ceilings but require proportionally more compute for SFT, RM training, and RLHF rollouts
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: evaluate minimum capable model size on task benchmarks before committing to alignment compute

conflict_axes.description: Optimizing for specific alignment benchmarks risks Goodhart inflation as models overfit benchmark artifacts; broader multi-metric eval resists but is more expensive
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: rotate benchmarks; include human eval and red-team alongside automated benchmarks

conflict_axes.description: RLAIF/CAI scales alignment cheaply using AI judges but risks circular bias when judge and policy are from the same model family
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use human feedback as quality anchor; audit AI feedback against human sample before full replacement

edge_cases.description: Preference data annotated on a different model's outputs than the model being aligned; distribution mismatch causes DPO or RM to learn spurious correlations
edge_cases.mitigation: collect preference data from target model's rollouts, not a proxy model
edge_cases.detection: measure distribution distance between annotation rollouts and training rollouts

edge_cases.description: KL constraint too tight blocks reward signal; model shows no alignment improvement despite training loss decreasing
edge_cases.mitigation: monitor reward trace alongside KL; loosen KL if reward plateau detected early
edge_cases.detection: reward score flat for >500 steps while KL is near zero

edge_cases.description: Reward hacking via length exploitation: policy learns that longer responses receive higher reward scores regardless of quality
edge_cases.mitigation: add length-normalized reward term; use length-controlled eval benchmarks
edge_cases.detection: monotone positive correlation between response length and reward score

edge_cases.description: DPO likelihood displacement: chosen response log-prob decreases during DPO training, indicating optimization collapse
edge_cases.mitigation: monitor chosen response log-prob; apply reference policy correction or use IPO variant
edge_cases.detection: chosen log-prob decreasing while rejected log-prob also decreasing

edge_cases.description: Benchmark contamination: alignment training data contains text from held-out benchmark evaluation sets, inflating measured performance
edge_cases.mitigation: decontaminate training data; use withheld benchmark versions
edge_cases.detection: n-gram overlap scan between training corpus and benchmark

edge_cases.description: RM overfitting to annotator artifacts: reward model learns to prefer formatting (bullet points, markdown) over substantive quality
edge_cases.mitigation: diversify annotators; add formatting-stripped comparison pairs
edge_cases.detection: RM scores plain vs formatted responses of equal quality - significant score gap flags artifact

edge_cases.description: Circular RLAIF feedback: AI judge used to label data is from the same model family as the model being aligned, propagating self-preferences
edge_cases.mitigation: use a different model family as AI judge; always validate against human sample
edge_cases.detection: AI judge preferences diverge from human preferences on calibration set

edge_cases.description: Safety over-refusal: safety alignment training causes model to refuse clearly benign requests, degrading helpfulness
edge_cases.mitigation: tune safety reward weight downward; add explicit non-refusal reward for benign prompts
edge_cases.detection: refusal rate on benign helpfulness benchmark exceeds 5%

edge_cases.description: RLVR reward exploitation: model learns to pass test cases by memorizing test patterns rather than solving the underlying problem
edge_cases.mitigation: use held-out test cases; add problem-level deduplication
edge_cases.detection: solve rate high on training test cases but fails on novel problem variants

edge_cases.description: Compute budget overrun during RLHF: rollout generation cost dominates and exceeds planned budget mid-training
edge_cases.mitigation: profile rollout cost before full run; use shorter rollout length or fewer iterations
edge_cases.detection: GPU cost tracking alerts when 50% of budget consumed at <50% of planned iterations

edge_cases.description: SFT-alignment distribution gap: SFT trained on distribution X but preference alignment collects data on distribution Y, causing reference policy KL miscalibration
edge_cases.mitigation: align SFT training data distribution with preference collection prompts
edge_cases.detection: KL divergence between SFT and aligned policy much higher than expected

edge_cases.description: PRM step boundary ambiguity: annotators disagree on where reasoning steps begin and end, causing noisy PRM training labels
edge_cases.mitigation: define explicit step boundary syntax; train annotators on step segmentation protocol
edge_cases.detection: inter-annotator agreement on step boundaries < 0.5 kappa

workflow.action: Base model selection and license review
SFT baseline training on instruction demonstrations
Prompt diversity design and annotation corpus construction
Human preference data collection with explain-then-choose protocol
Preference data quality filtering and deduplication
KL budget configuration and reference policy freezing
RLHF PPO training with reward hacking monitoring
gates: no hacking patterns in rollout audit
red-team pass rate < 5% on harm categories

workflow.action: Safety alignment pass and over-refusal calibration
Deployment guardrail configuration and monitoring setup

dominance_rules.rule: Data quality dominates data quantity for reward model training
dominance_rules.rationale: RM trained on high-agreement pairs outperforms RM trained on 10x noisy pairs

dominance_rules.rule: KL constraint must be set before RLHF training starts; cannot be retroactively tightened without restart
dominance_rules.rationale: Post-hoc KL tightening changes the effective optimization landscape and invalidates the training run
dominance_rules.applies_when: KL budget not configured before PPO run

dominance_rules.rule: Human eval win-rate dominates automated benchmark scores for deployment decisions
dominance_rules.rationale: Benchmarks are proxy measures subject to Goodhart; human eval reflects true alignment quality
dominance_rules.applies_when: automated benchmark and human eval disagree

dominance_rules.rule: RLVR verifiable reward dominates learned RM for math/code domains
dominance_rules.rationale: Ground-truth verification has zero Goodhart risk; learned RM is an unnecessary approximation when verification is available
dominance_rules.applies_when: task domain has cheap automated verification

dominance_rules.rule: Base model license compliance is a hard gate before any fine-tuning investment
dominance_rules.rationale: License violation discovered after fine-tuning investment causes complete loss of work
dominance_rules.applies_when: base model not legally cleared for use case

dominance_rules.rule: SFT baseline must complete before RLHF or DPO; RL from base model is unstable
dominance_rules.rationale: InstructGPT ablation shows SFT warm-start is necessary for PPO stability and quality

dominance_rules.rule: Safety alignment gates outperform helpfulness in all deployment decisions when the two conflict
dominance_rules.rationale: Harmful outputs have asymmetric downside risk vs unhelpful outputs in production
dominance_rules.applies_when: safety and helpfulness metrics conflict at deployment gate

dominance_rules.rule: DPO preferred over RLHF when compute budget prohibits full RL pipeline
dominance_rules.rationale: DPO achieves competitive alignment at 3-5x lower compute; budget constraint overrides quality maximization

dominance_rules.rule: Reward hacking detection triggers training halt before alignment eval is trusted
dominance_rules.rationale: Evaluating a hacked policy produces misleading metrics that propagate to deployment decisions
dominance_rules.applies_when: reward hacking signal detected in rollout audit

dominance_rules.rule: Outcome RM must be trained before PRM; PRM adds step granularity on top of outcome baseline
dominance_rules.rationale: PRM without outcome RM anchor has no quality reference for step correctness
dominance_rules.applies_when: PRM training planned without outcome RM

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not restart SFT when only preference data changes; SFT checkpoint is reusable across alignment algorithm changes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: SFT training is expensive; preference data changes only affect RM/DPO downstream

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not retrain reward model for minor KL coefficient changes; RM is independent of PPO hyperparameters
anti_rework_rules.rationale: RM training and PPO hyperparameter tuning are orthogonal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not re-collect all preference data when only a small domain gap is identified; targeted domain-specific collection suffices
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Full re-annotation is unnecessary when coverage gap is localized

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not re-run full RLHF when DPO achieves sufficient alignment quality; avoid RL overhead when simpler method works
anti_rework_rules.rationale: DPO achieves competitive quality at much lower cost; only escalate to RLHF if DPO fails quality gate
anti_rework_rules.trigger_to_ignore: DPO quality within 5% of RLHF target

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not re-run base model capability benchmarks after alignment; SFT/alignment does not change base architecture
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Capability benchmarks characterize the base model; re-running wastes compute

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not rebuild deployment guardrails when only reward model checkpoint is updated without policy change
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Guardrail classifiers depend on policy output distribution, not RM internals
anti_rework_rules.trigger_to_ignore: RM checkpoint update without policy change

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not re-run full safety alignment pass for minor preference data updates; targeted safety DPO pass on new harm categories suffices
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Full safety pass is expensive; incremental targeted pass covers new categories without full reset

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not re-design prompt distribution for each iteration of online RLHF; only expand when coverage audit finds new gap
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Prompt redesign is expensive; online rounds sample from existing distribution unless audit flags gap
anti_rework_rules.trigger_to_ignore: new online RLHF round without coverage gap

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not recompute Goodhart monitor from scratch after each training step; sample-based periodic audits suffice
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Continuous Goodhart monitoring is impractical; periodic cadence with triggered full audits is sufficient

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not re-filter synthetic preference data when human data quality filter threshold changes; synthetic filtering uses separate quality criteria
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Synthetic and human data have different quality distributions; human filter changes do not propagate to synthetic

iteration_protocol.action: halt RLHF training, audit rollouts for hacking patterns, retune KL or refresh RM

iteration_protocol.trigger: DPO likelihood displacement detected (chosen log-prob decreasing)
iteration_protocol.action: switch to IPO variant or reduce DPO learning rate; re-check reference policy alignment
reduce PPO step size, tighten clip range, or restart with lower KL coefficient

iteration_protocol.trigger: Annotation IAA drops below 0.5 on audit
iteration_protocol.action: revise annotation guidelines, retrain annotators, re-annotate low-agreement subset

iteration_protocol.trigger: Win-rate vs SFT stagnates across two RLHF iterations
iteration_protocol.action: switch from offline to online RLHF; refresh RM on policy rollouts

iteration_protocol.trigger: Benchmark contamination detected in training data
iteration_protocol.action: decontaminate training corpus, use withheld benchmark version, re-run eval

iteration_protocol.trigger: Over-refusal rate exceeds 5% on benign helpfulness benchmark
iteration_protocol.action: reduce safety reward weight, add explicit non-refusal reward for benign prompts, re-run safety pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: RLVR solve rate plateaus for 3 consecutive checkpoints
iteration_protocol.action: expand verifiable reward domain, add PRM step-level signal, or switch to outcome+process reward combination

iteration_protocol.trigger: Production anomaly detected by deployment guardrail
iteration_protocol.action: root-cause analysis, targeted red-team on anomaly category, patch guardrail or trigger safety re-alignment

iteration_protocol.trigger: Synthetic data quality filter detects distribution collapse (all outputs similar)
iteration_protocol.action: diversify teacher model prompts, increase sampling temperature, revert to human data only

priority_rationale: Base model selection is the highest-irreversibility decision; preference data and SFT are prerequisites for all alignment methods; reward modeling and RLHF are the core alignment mechanisms; safety and evaluation gates before deployment; DPO/RLVR/PRM are alternatives evaluated after core pipeline; iterative and synthetic methods are improvements on top of working baseline

validation_protocol.structural_check: all required keys present at top level and node/edge level
validation_protocol.ref_resolution: all evidence_refs, competency_question_refs, conflict_axis_refs resolve to defined ids
validation_protocol.count_checks: 19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow, 10-14 competency_questions, 7-12 dominance_rules, 7-12 anti_rework_rules, 6-10 iteration_protocol
validation_protocol.high_risk_obligations: nodes with risk_if_wrong>=0.80 must have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
validation_protocol.high_coupling_obligations: nodes with cross_topic_coupling>=0.75 must have non-empty revisit_triggers
validation_protocol.conflict_edge_obligations: conflict edges must have signed_tension<0 and non-empty resolution_rule
validation_protocol.dependency_acyclicity: dependency edges must form a DAG
validation_protocol.priority_order_completeness: priority_order must list every node id exactly once
validation_protocol.derived_fields_zero: all derived fields set to 0 before formula tool run

test_cases.input_summary: single prompt pool, SFT baseline, DPO alignment
reward score increases but human preference decreases
safety RLHF pass increases refusal rate above 5% threshold
RLHF compute cost exceeds budget by 2x
